correctness.rationale: For every zero rook cell, r_i+c_j=2 is exactly the closed labeling condition because neighbor sum excludes its own zero label. A zero row and zero column cannot coexist. Square case: n minimum weight forces every row and column sum 1, yielding n! permutation matrices. For 2<=m<n, all rows and columns positive if weight<2m; any row sum>=2 must be completely positive (since positive columns forbid zeros), yielding weight>=n+m-1>=2m, whereas all row sums 1 contradict n positive columns. For equality: a zero column forces all row sums 2 and only fully filled columns, hence one 2-column or two 1-columns. With no zero columns, the weight bound h(n-1)<=m forces a single all-one full row at n=m+1; zero equations force nonheavy rows to select a common column. Independently reconstructed definition-level bounded cases (m,n)=(2,2),(2,3),(2,4),(2,5),(3,3),(3,4),(3,5), matching counts 2,12,10,15,6,22,15 and no lower weight; finite cases only corroborate all-parameter proof.
